findings.title: Legacy directory custody hash has ambiguous path/content framing before mirror deletion.
findings.assessment: _dir_tree_sha256 concatenates each relative filename and raw contents without lengths or separators. A one-file tree a:"bc" and ab:"c" encode identical bytes. The same digest guards shutil.rmtree of a mirror, so hash equality need not imply equal path-to-byte populations. This is an encoding collision, not a SHA-256 collision.
findings.limits: No files were created/deleted for this control.

findings.title: Legacy harvest and lifecycle declarations are weaker than the main archive journal.

Corrupt secondary corpus manifests are swallowed as empty before replacement. Lifecycle request hardcodes producer_lease_active false and treats absent parser gaps as complete extraction, with empty evidence_refs for findings. In contrast, main archive operations perform journal/seal checks.
findings.limits: No archive/lifecycle method executed. Parsing completeness is not semantic completeness; no historical source loss is inferred from current code alone.

findings.title: Legacy paper miners can turn empty, unreadable or contradictory reports into PASS.
findings.assessment: Markdown status searches PASSED/CLEARED before BLOCKED/NOT READY and disregards chronology/negation. OMC/fallback paths can retain empty or failed parse inputs then return PASS from lack of recorded failures; OMC DTO defaults science/code checks to passing unless supplied. Some PASS declarations become THEOREMS_VERIFIED without proof replay. Newer extraction has explicit gap handling, so these older owners must not be treated as equivalent.
findings.limits: No source paper or retained miner executed; mathematical validity is not inferred from either PASS or parser failure.
findings.next_action: Require known schema, explicit observed checks and readable complete population; preserve UNKNOWN/UNREADABLE and use typed status precedence.

findings.title: Research event mirror checks length but not the retained prefix bytes.
findings.assessment: _mirror_events counts newlines then appends events after that count. Equal-count edited lines survive without comparison to checkpoint events; a longer mirror is refused but same-length corruption is not. Checkpoint/native event verification is a separate boundary and may still detect its own mutations.

findings.title: Native binary digest cache can return stale hashes after metadata-preserving mutation.
findings.assessment: The cache key is absolute path, mtime_ns and size. Different same-length bytes with preserved mtime receive the old SHA; _host uses that result in its native binary binding. This is narrower than arbitrary path replacement and does not prove a historical untrusted binary was executed.
findings.limits: Source/body review; no end-to-end native or provider execution.
findings.next_action: Hash actual admitted bytes at the invocation boundary or bind an immutable opened file/content-addressed binary; do not use mutable filesystem metadata as integrity identity.

findings.title: Diff/oracle execution can check transformed bytes while labeling the original candidate hash.
findings.assessment: The adapter hashes raw candidate bytes, decodes with replacement and writes text to the temporary source path; invalid UTF-8 and platform newline conversion can change executed bytes. The critique service also hashes UTF-8 diff text then writes it using platform text translation. The original test/base code is intentionally supplied to the proposer, so this is a public repair exercise, not a sealed independent benchmark.

findings.title: Multi-round critique trusts returned oracle verdict without rechecking candidate identity.
findings.assessment: After check_candidate, the service branches on verdict and persists returned receipt, but does not compare its candidate ID/bytes/hash to the current candidate. A stale or misbound injected checker result can therefore be recorded as accepted here. The concrete checker may bind these correctly; this is a missing use-case boundary check, not a demonstrated production native bypass. Caller extra context can also override prepared test/base/workspace keys.

findings.title: Default append-only DDC sink does not restore existing head or commit memory after disk success.
findings.assessment: Constructor resets sequence0/headNone even for an existing output file. record_step mutates lists/head/sequence before a fallible append; failure returns Err after in-memory advancement. Reopening can append a second genesis and failed writes can leave memory/disk divergent. The stronger genealogy store separately rereads and validates its chain; its guarantees cannot be transferred to this sink.
findings.limits: Source/body review; no end-to-end native or provider execution.

findings.title: Qualification receipts encode asserted independence and leave cross-subject bindings to callers.
findings.assessment: N1/N2/N4 receipt admission checks booleans, worker counts and evidence shapes rather than replaying independent probes. The ladder combines passing receipts without one common subject/snapshot/patch identity. Selection checks epoch ID and hard-gate sets but can miss weights/probes or duplicate gate IDs; the orchestration owner has stronger full bindings. These interfaces are useful DTOs, not sufficient qualification certificates.

findings.title: Mutable antibody/catalog state has path and stale-admission hazards.
findings.assessment: Legacy catalog/pharmacy helpers form paths from unvalidated antibody identifiers. Default antibody cache is loaded once and can miss external revocation; recording candidates can overwrite existing status. Cemetery candidate publication uses read-modify-write so atomic replace alone does not prevent overwriting a concurrent admission. Newer typed admission paths remain stronger and must not be conflated.

findings.title: Scheduler completion and swarm echo helpers do not measure actual task progress.
findings.assessment: finish_bout derives statuses/routes from supplied completion rather than task evidence and emits changed_state1 for synthetic traversal. run_swarm helpers include a synchronous echo implementation with an infinite_timeout label whose timeout is unused. These can demonstrate choreography, but are not bounded worker execution or measured workflow success.

findings.title: Request value-object equality and hashing use incompatible representations.
findings.assessment: carrier_context equality uses ordinary dict equality, where {x:1} equals {x:True}; hash converts values to strings, which differ. Nested mutable dicts also undermine stable hashes of frozen dataclasses. Equal values can have unequal hashes and later mutate under the same object identity.
findings.limits: Source/body review; no end-to-end native or provider execution.
